title: How Not to Age: The Scientific Approach to Getting Healthier as You Get Older

contents: Part I — Slowing Eleven Pathways of Aging
Part II — The Optimal Anti-Aging Regimen
The Red, White, and Blue Zone
Lifestyle: Exercise, Weight Control, Sleep, Stress Management, and Social Ties
Preserving Your Bowel and Bladder Function
Part IV — Dr. Greger's Anti-Aging Eight

audiences: Readers seeking a broad reference on nutrition, lifestyle, ageing biology, and maintaining function
People attracted to whole-food plant-predominant eating who want mechanisms and extensive references
Older or middle-aged readers comparing popular longevity interventions with a sceptical supplement review
Health communicators who can separate exploratory mechanisms from human outcome evidence

sources.title: How Not to Age
sources.supports: Author's purpose, four-part design, eleven-pathway model, centenarian framing, function chapters, and Anti-Aging Eight.
sources.limitations: Publisher-hosted introduction excerpt, not the uninterrupted full book.

sources.title: How Not to Age
sources.author_or_publisher: Michael Greger; Flatiron Books via Google Books
sources.supports: Title, author, publisher, date, ebook ISBN, length, subjects, preview, and central claims.
sources.limitations: Limited preview and edition length differs from print records.

sources.title: How Not to Age
sources.supports: Print identity, 2023 publication, hardcover ISBN, physical extent, subject, and complete part and chapter contents.
sources.limitations: Catalogue metadata and syndicated summary, not content evaluation.

sources.title: Supplemental Videos for How Not to Age
sources.supports: Chapter-by-chapter topic index, linked supplemental material, interventions considered, and the book's external citation system.
sources.limitations: Author-controlled companion material; volume does not establish evidential strength.

sources.title: Hallmarks of Aging: An Expanding Universe
sources.supports: Independent twelve-hallmark framework, mechanism definitions, intervention criteria, and interconnectedness of ageing processes.
sources.limitations: Mechanistic framework; does not show that particular foods change human lifespan.

sources.title: Promoting Physical Activity and Healthy Diets for Healthy Ageing
sources.author_or_publisher: World Health Organization Regional Office for Europe
sources.supports: Healthy-ageing focus on functional ability, diet, aerobic and strength activity, balance, independence, heterogeneity, and malnutrition.
sources.limitations: Population guidance, not an audit of every book claim.

sources.title: Healthy Diet
sources.supports: Independent principles of adequacy, balance, moderation, diversity, whole grains, pulses, fruit, vegetables, and fibre.
sources.limitations: General guidance, not a strict vegan or longevity-specific prescription.

sources.title: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour
sources.supports: Independent aerobic, strength, balance, sedentary, disability, and older-adult activity recommendations.
sources.limitations: Population guidance rather than individual prescription.

sources.title: Evidence-Based Recommendations for Optimal Dietary Protein Intake in Older People
sources.author_or_publisher: PROT-AGE Study Group; Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
sources.supports: Expert recommendation of 1.0–1.2 grams of protein per kilogram daily for most older adults and more during activity or illness.
sources.limitations: Consensus position from 2013; needs individual adjustment, including kidney disease.

sources.title: Body-Composition Changes in the CALERIE-2 Study
sources.author_or_publisher: Sai Krupa Das et al.; American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
sources.supports: Two-year human randomised calorie-restriction results, including reduced fat and fat-free mass and uncertainty about healthspan.
sources.limitations: Non-obese adults aged 21–51; not a lifespan trial or direct study of frail older adults.

sources.title: Plant-Based Diet and Risk of All-Cause Mortality
sources.author_or_publisher: Junwen Tan et al.; Frontiers in Nutrition
sources.supports: Meta-analysis associating healthier plant-based patterns with lower all-cause, cardiovascular, and cancer mortality.
sources.limitations: High heterogeneity and largely observational exposure; plant-based indices vary.

sources.title: Fish Consumption in Multiple Health Outcomes
sources.author_or_publisher: Mousa Shab-Bidar et al.; Advances in Nutrition
sources.supports: Umbrella review finding several moderate- or high-quality beneficial fish associations, including all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.
sources.limitations: Much evidence remains observational; sustainability, contaminants, preparation, and substitution vary.

sources.title: Nutrient Intake and Status in Adults Consuming Plant-Based Diets Compared to Meat-Eaters
sources.supports: Strengths of plant diets and lower B12, calcium, iodine, vitamin D, zinc, iron, EPA/DHA, and bone-density measures requiring planning or supplementation.
sources.limitations: Mixed observational and intervention studies across varied dietary definitions.

sources.title: Effects of Spermidine Supplementation on Cognition and Biomarkers in Older Adults
sources.author_or_publisher: Claudia Schwarz et al.; JAMA Network Open
sources.supports: Twelve-month randomised trial finding no significant primary memory or biomarker benefit from a spermidine-rich supplement.
sources.limitations: One dose, supplement, outcome set, and at-risk group; does not test whole spermidine-rich foods or lifespan.

sources.title: The Validity of Blue Zones Demography: A Response to Critiques
sources.author_or_publisher: Steven N. Austad and Giovanni M. Pes; The Gerontologist
sources.supports: Defence of formal age-validation methods used for defined Blue Zone populations and acknowledgement of historical false longevity claims.
sources.limitations: Authors defend a contested field and validation does not establish which lifestyle caused longevity.

sources.title: How Not to Age
sources.supports: Independent reception, scientific style, scepticism, optimism, breadth, single-study claims, function section, and print data.
sources.limitations: Trade review rather than full evidence audit.

sources.title: How Not to Age
sources.supports: Professional summary of the book's anti-ageing argument, food interventions, audience, and scale.
sources.limitations: Short collection-development review.

sources.title: Review of How Not to Age
sources.supports: Full-book account of structure, technicality, anti-supplement scepticism, function coverage, density, recommendation overload, and plant-based foundation.
sources.limitations: Reviewer shares the book's vegan orientation and is mostly favourable.

sources.title: How Not to Age by Dr. Michael Greger: Review and Summary
sources.supports: Detailed critical reading of editing, calorie and protein restriction, fish, exercise, function chapters, and claim interpretation.
sources.limitations: Uses a proprietary longevity score and makes some overly precise life-year estimates.

sources.title: How Not to Age
sources.supports: Large reader aggregate and recurring praise for evidence and actionability alongside complaints about density, length, and technical narration.
sources.limitations: Self-selected readers, merged editions, no control for expertise or completion.

workflow.coverage_notes: The full contents, publisher introduction, searchable preview, chapter-indexed companion material, and detailed full-book reviews cover all four parts. Central recommendations were checked against current ageing, diet, activity, protein, calorie-restriction, plant-nutrient, fish, Blue Zone, and spermidine evidence. No uninterrupted lawful full text was used.
next_steps: Optional: compare every one of the book's thousands of citations against an owner-supplied copy and current systematic reviews before promoting coverage to full-book.
